## sigma_rule_info(rule_yaml)

Parses a [Sigma](https://sigmahq.io) rule (YAML) and returns a single row of its header metadata: `title`, `id`, `level`, `status`, `description`, logsource `product`/`service`, and the rule's `tags` (a `VARCHAR[]`, typically MITRE ATT&CK references like `attack.t1110`).

**When to use it.** Triage and catalog rules without evaluating them against events -- e.g. build an inventory of a rule repository, filter by severity `level`, group by logsource `product`, or expand `tags` with `UNNEST` to map coverage against MITRE ATT&CK.

**Inputs.** `rule_yaml` -- a complete Sigma rule (positional). Like every rule here it needs a non-empty `logsource:` block.

**Output & edge cases.** A table function returning exactly one row. A NULL rule yields **no rows**; a malformed rule raises a clear parse error (this is an introspection helper run against a known rule, not a per-row scan). Header fields absent from the rule come back NULL.

# sigma_rule_info

Returns one row of header metadata for a Sigma rule -- the human-facing fields you would show in a rule catalog or triage view.

## Usage

Pass a rule and project the header columns you need (`title`, `level`, ...), or expand the `tags` list with `UNNEST` to map MITRE ATT&CK coverage. Fully runnable, catalog-qualified queries are attached as example queries.

## Notes

- One row per rule; a NULL rule yields no rows.
- A malformed rule raises a clear parse error.
- The `tags` column is a `VARCHAR[]` (use `UNNEST` to expand it).
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Read a rule's title and severity level from its header.", "sql": "SELECT title, level FROM sigma.main.sigma_rule_info('{title: T, level: high, logsource: {service: security}, detection: {sel: {EventID: 1}, condition: sel}}')"}, {"description": "Expand a rule's MITRE ATT&CK tags into one row per tag.", "sql": "SELECT UNNEST(tags) AS tag FROM sigma.main.sigma_rule_info('{title: T, tags: [attack.t1110], logsource: {service: security}, detection: {sel: {EventID: 1}, condition: sel}}')"}]

## sigma_match_fields(rule_yaml)

Returns one row per distinct event field that a [Sigma](https://sigmahq.io) rule keys on (e.g. `EventID`, `LogonType`, `Image`). It answers 'what columns does this rule actually look at?' without evaluating the rule against any data.

**When to use it.** Plan indexes and storage coverage: discover which log fields must be present and indexed for a rule to be evaluable, audit a fleet of rules for a common field set, or detect rules that reference fields your pipeline does not collect.

**Inputs.** `rule_yaml` -- a complete Sigma rule (positional), with a non-empty `logsource:` block.

**Output & edge cases.** A table function emitting one `field` row per referenced field. A NULL rule yields **no rows**; a malformed rule raises a clear parse error. Bare-keyword conditions (which match anywhere in the event rather than a named field) contribute no field rows.

## sigma_check(rule_yaml)

Returns `true` when a [Sigma](https://sigmahq.io) rule (YAML) parses and compiles successfully using only features this worker supports, and `false` otherwise. Unlike `sigma_match`, it **never raises** -- it is the safe, boolean-returning gate you run before trusting a rule.

**When to use it.** Validate rules in bulk -- e.g. lint a column of candidate rules, filter a detection-rule repository down to the ones this engine can actually evaluate, or guard a pipeline with `WHERE sigma.sigma_check(rule_text)` before feeding rules to `sigma_match`.

**Inputs.** `rule_yaml` -- a complete Sigma rule. Remember that pySigma requires a non-empty `logsource:` block; a rule missing it (or with `logsource: {}`) is invalid and returns `false`.

**Output & edge cases.** Returns `BOOLEAN`; NULL in, NULL out. It returns `false` for malformed YAML, a missing `logsource:`, a missing `condition`, or any unsupported modifier. Because it swallows errors into `false`, use `sigma_rule_info` if you need the specific parse error surfaced.

# sigma_check

A non-raising validator: returns `true` when a Sigma rule parses and compiles with only supported features, `false` otherwise.

## Usage

Run it over a column of candidate rules to keep (or reject) the ones this engine can evaluate before feeding them to `sigma_match`. Fully runnable, catalog-qualified queries are attached as example queries.

## Arguments

| name | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `rule_yaml` | VARCHAR | A Sigma rule (YAML) to validate. |

## Notes

- A rule **must** have a non-empty `logsource:` block, or it is invalid.
- Never raises -- malformed or unsupported rules simply return `false`.
- NULL in, NULL out.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "A well-formed rule with a logsource and condition validates as true.", "sql": "SELECT sigma.main.sigma_check('{title: Failed Logon, logsource: {service: security}, detection: {selection: {EventID: 4625}, condition: selection}}')"}, {"description": "A rule that is not valid Sigma YAML returns false rather than raising.", "sql": "SELECT sigma.main.sigma_check('not a valid rule')"}]
rows.vgi.title: Sigma Rule Validity Check

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## sigma_match(event_json, rule_yaml)

Tests whether a single log/event row, supplied as a JSON object string, matches a [Sigma](https://sigmahq.io) detection rule supplied as YAML. This is the headline function of the catalog: it turns 'detection-as-code' into a SQL predicate so you can hunt for a known threat across an entire log table.

**When to use it.** Apply it per row over a log column to find matching events, typically in a `WHERE` clause: `WHERE sigma.sigma_match(to_json(t), :rule)`. The rule is parsed and compiled exactly once per distinct rule string (the engine is `lru_cache`-d), so scanning one constant rule across millions of rows compiles a single time and then evaluates the boolean condition tree per row.

**Inputs.** `event_json` — the event as a JSON object string (e.g. from `to_json(row)`); `rule_yaml` — a complete Sigma rule, which must include a non-empty `logsource:` block and a `detection:` section with a `condition`.

**Output & edge cases.** Returns `BOOLEAN`. A NULL input row yields NULL. A malformed *event* JSON yields `false` (one bad log row is a non-match, never a crash), but a malformed or unsupported *rule* raises a clear error so you never silently mis-evaluate. Supported leaf forms include field/value comparisons (equals, contains, startswith, endswith, regex, wildcards) and bare keyword searches; selector forms like `1 of selection_*` and `all of them` are expanded by pySigma and work for free.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# sigma_match

Returns `true` when a JSON event matches a Sigma detection rule. It is the core matcher for SIEM-style threat detection directly in SQL.

## Usage

Apply it per row over a log column -- typically in a `WHERE` clause against `to_json(row)` -- to keep only the events a rule matches. Fully runnable, catalog-qualified queries are attached as example queries.

## Arguments

| name | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `event_json` | VARCHAR | The event as a JSON object string. |
| `rule_yaml` | VARCHAR | A Sigma rule (YAML) with a non-empty `logsource:`. |

## Notes

- A malformed *event* returns `false`; a malformed *rule* raises a clear error.
- NULL in, NULL out.
- The rule compiles once per distinct string, then evaluates per row, so a constant rule over a whole column is cheap.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "A failed-logon event matches a rule requiring EventID 4625.", "sql": "SELECT sigma.main.sigma_match('{\"EventID\": 4625, \"LogonType\": 3}', '{title: Failed Network Logon, logsource: {service: security}, detection: {selection: {EventID: 4625}, condition: selection}}')"}, {"description": "Hunt per row over an inline log table, keeping only matching events.", "sql": "SELECT event FROM (VALUES ('{\"EventID\": 4625, \"LogonType\": 3}'), ('{\"EventID\": 1}')) AS logs(event) WHERE sigma.main.sigma_match(event, '{title: Failed Network Logon, logsource: {service: security}, detection: {selection: {EventID: 4625, LogonType: 3}, condition: selection}}')"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description": "A failed-logon event (EventID 4625, network logon type 3) matches a brute-force detection rule.", "sql": "SELECT sigma.main.sigma_match('{\"EventID\": 4625, \"LogonType\": 3}', '{title: Failed Network Logon, logsource: {service: security}, detection: {selection: {EventID: 4625, LogonType: 3}, condition: selection}}') AS matched"}, {"description": "An unrelated process-creation event does not match the same rule.", "sql": "SELECT sigma.main.sigma_match('{\"EventID\": 1}', '{title: Failed Network Logon, logsource: {service: security}, detection: {selection: {EventID: 4625, LogonType: 3}, condition: selection}}') AS matched"}, {"description": "Apply the matcher per row over an inline log table -- the headline hunting pattern.", "sql": "SELECT event, sigma.main.sigma_match(event, '{title: Failed Network Logon, logsource: {service: security}, detection: {selection: {EventID: 4625, LogonType: 3}, condition: selection}}') AS matched FROM (VALUES ('{\"EventID\": 4625, \"LogonType\": 3}'), ('{\"EventID\": 1}')) AS logs(event) ORDER BY matched"}]
rows.vgi.title: Sigma Rule Event Match

rows: SELECT sigma.main.sigma_match('{"EventID": 4625, "LogonType": 3}', '{title: Failed Network Logon, logsource: {service: security}, detection: {selection: {EventID: 4625}, condition: selection}}')

SELECT event FROM (VALUES ('{"EventID": 4625, "LogonType": 3}'), ('{"EventID": 1}')) AS logs(event) WHERE sigma.main.sigma_match(event, '{title: Failed Network Logon, logsource: {service: security}, detection: {selection: {EventID: 4625, LogonType: 3}, condition: selection}}')
